booking.name: Booking.com
booking.description: Search Booking.com properties and retrieve prices, review scores, star ratings, room and bed configuration, availability and grouped filters in JSON.

params.name: q
params.doc: The destination to search for: a city, region, district, landmark, or specific property name (e.g. Dubrovnik). Optional when both dest_id and dest_type are supplied, since those identify the destination on their own.

params.name: dest_id
params.doc: The Booking destination id, obtained from the Booking Autocomplete API. Combine with dest_type to target an exact destination instead of relying on the q text match. The two identify a destination only as a pair, so either both are sent or neither is; one on its own is rejected with a 400.

params.name: dest_type
params.doc: The type of the dest_id destination, returned alongside it by the Autocomplete API. One of city, region, country, district, hotel, airport or landmark. A hotel destination searches that property's area with the property ranked first, rather than returning it alone. Must be sent together with dest_id; one without the other is a 400.

params.name: check_in_date
params.doc: The check-in date in YYYY-MM-DD format. It is rejected with a 400 unless it is sent together with check_out_date, is a real calendar date, and is not already past in Etc/GMT+12 — the last time zone on earth to roll a date over. Prices are quoted for a specific stay, so price, extracted_price, nightly_price and extracted_nightly_price are returned only when a date range (or the flexible-date parameters) is supplied. A dateless search returns property metadata without pricing.

params.name: check_out_date
params.doc: The check-out date in YYYY-MM-DD format. It is rejected with a 400 unless it is sent together with check_in_date, is a real calendar date that is not already past in Etc/GMT+12, falls strictly later than check_in_date, and leaves a stay of no more than 90 nights.

params.name: flex_window
params.doc: Enables flexible-date search, widening the stay by ± the given number of days around check_in_date / check_out_date. Supported values: 1, 2, 3, 7.

params.name: flex_months
params.doc: Search whole months instead of fixed dates, Booking's “When do you want to go?”. A comma-separated list of up to 3 months in YYYY-MM format (e.g. 2026-09,2026-10,2026-11). Must be used together with flex_stay_length, and cannot be combined with check_in_date, check_out_date or flex_window.

params.name: flex_stay_length
params.doc: How long the stay should be, per Booking's “How long do you want to stay?”. One of weekend, week, month, or a number of nights between 1 and 30. Required when flex_months is set.

params.name: flex_start_day
params.doc: The day of the week the stay starts on: monday … sunday. Booking always pins flexible searches to a single start weekday, so a default is applied when this is omitted; results only include stays beginning on that day.

params.name: adults
params.doc: The number of adult guests. An integer between 1 and 30.

params.name: children_ages
params.doc: A comma-separated list of the children's ages, each between 0 and 17 (e.g. 5,8). The number of values sets the number of children; an age outside that range is a 400.

params.name: rooms
params.doc: The number of rooms to search for. An integer between 1 and 30.

params.name: sort_by
params.doc: The ordering of the property results. Unset by default: with no sort_by, no ordering parameter is sent and none is echoed back in search_parameters, and Booking applies its own ordering, which is by popularity. Available options: popularity

params.name: filters
params.doc: A comma-separated list of facet tokens to refine the results. Each token is the value of an option in the response's filters block (e.g. class=5 for 5-star properties, fc=2 for free cancellation). Combine multiple tokens with commas. Same-group tokens broaden the results (OR), cross-group tokens narrow them (AND). The price group is a range rather than a checkbox: it reports min, max and currency alongside a full-range token, so you can substitute your own bounds as price=USD-300-2000-1.

params.name: currency
params.doc: The ISO currency code the prices are returned in (e.g. EUR, GBP). Check the full list of supported Booking.com currency values. When omitted, Booking prices the results in its own default for the request, which is not guaranteed to be stable between calls.

params.name: language
params.doc: The interface language of the search (e.g. en-us, de, fr). Booking encodes it in the request path, so the value you send is the language you get back. Check the full list of supported Booking.com language values. Affects result language and number formatting.

params.name: page
params.doc: The results page to retrieve. Booking pages in blocks of 25, though a page may render a few more or fewer; use the pagination.next_page value from the response to page forward. Requesting a page past the last one returns an empty properties array together with search_information.total_results. Not supported together with flex_months and flex_stay_length.

booking_autocomplete.name: Booking.com Autocomplete
booking_autocomplete.description: Autocomplete Booking.com destinations (cities, regions, airports, landmarks, properties) with the dest_id and dest_type a property search needs, in JSON.

params.name: q
params.doc: The partial or full destination text to autocomplete, up to 200 characters (e.g. dubro). Returns matching cities, regions, countries, districts, airports, landmarks and individual properties. Each suggestion carries the dest_id and dest_type the Booking.com API takes; note that a hotel suggestion searches that property's area with it ranked first rather than returning it alone.

params.name: num
params.doc: How many suggestions to return. By default, it returns 5. You can return up to 100 suggestions.

params.name: language
params.doc: A hint for the language the suggestion titles and labels come back in (e.g. de, fr). Booking resolves the language from the query itself, so language only applies where the query leaves it open — searching Parigi returns Italian whatever language says. It also affects which destinations Booking ranks into the list, not only their labels, so pin it when you need a stable suggestion set. Check the full list of supported Booking.com language values.

booking_property.name: Booking.com Property
booking_property.description: Retrieve a Booking.com property's rooms, amenities, review breakdown, house rules, FAQs and nearby restaurants, attractions and transport in JSON.

params.name: url
params.doc: The Booking.com property page URL (e.g. https://www.booking.com/hotel/hr/city-residences.html). Obtain it from the properties[].link field of a Booking.com API response.

params.name: check_in_date
params.doc: The check-in date in YYYY-MM-DD format. Determines the room rates and availability shown for the stay. It is rejected with a 400 unless it is sent together with check_out_date, is a real calendar date, and is not already past in Etc/GMT+12 — the last time zone on earth to roll a date over. Booking prices a stay rather than a date, so the rooms array is returned only when both dates are supplied, and is omitted when the property has no availability for the requested stay.

params.name: check_out_date
params.doc: The check-out date in YYYY-MM-DD format. It is rejected with a 400 unless it is sent together with check_in_date, is a real calendar date that is not already past in Etc/GMT+12, falls strictly later than check_in_date, and leaves a stay of no more than 90 nights.

params.name: adults
params.doc: The number of adult guests. An integer between 1 and 30.

params.name: children_ages
params.doc: A comma-separated list of the children's ages, each between 0 and 17 (e.g. 5,8). The number of values sets the number of children; an age outside that range is a 400.

params.name: rooms
params.doc: The number of rooms to search for. An integer between 1 and 30.

params.name: currency
params.doc: The ISO currency code the room prices are returned in (e.g. EUR, GBP). Check the full list of supported Booking.com currency values. When omitted, Booking prices the page in its own default for the request, which is not guaranteed to be stable between calls.

params.name: language
params.doc: The language of the returned property content (e.g. de, fr): room names, amenities, house rules and review categories. Booking encodes it in the property URL path, so the value you send is the language you get back. Check the full list of supported Booking.com language values. Defaults to en-us — Booking's own default English — rather than being left to Booking, so the same request returns the same language every time.

chatgpt.name: ChatGPT
chatgpt.description: Query ChatGPT through a simple API and get back a structured answer, the model that answered, and cited web sources when web search is enabled.

params.name: q
params.doc: The prompt to send to ChatGPT. Up to 4000 characters.

params.name: web_search
params.doc: Set to true to use ChatGPT with web search. ChatGPT runs a live web search and answers with cited sources, turning the request into a ChatGPT search API. The pages the answer cites are returned in reference_links, and the full ranked set of pages ChatGPT retrieved is returned in web_results. ChatGPT may also search on its own initiative, so these can appear without this parameter. response_metadata.is_web_search_performed always reports whether a search actually ran.

params.name: expand_entities
params.doc: Set to true to expand each knowledge-entity card in the answer into a rich detail card with a description, titled sections, related entities ("Key Areas" / "Nearby Landmarks"), inline images, and reference links, returned under each card's details. Adds latency since each entity triggers an extra fetch.

duckduckgo.name: DuckDuckGo
duckduckgo.description: Scrape DuckDuckGo for organic results, ads, ai overview, images, videos, knowledge graph and more. Retrieve detailed app data in JSON format.

params.name: q
params.doc: This parameter is used for the terms you want to search on DuckDuckGo. Queries can include operators and advanced filters like "machine learning models", site:, intitle:, or inurl:.

params.name: locale
params.doc: Specifies the country and language for your search. The default parameter is us-en. Check the full list of supported DuckDuckGo locales.

params.name: safe
params.doc: Specifies the filter level for adult content. Available values are: on Default

params.name: time_period
params.doc: Filters results by date. Predefined values are: any_time Default

params.name: next_page_token
params.doc: This parameter is used to retrieve the next page of results. It is returned in the response when there are more results to display. The next_page_token is a unique identifier for the next page of results. It is used to retrieve the next page of results.

duckduckgo_images.name: DuckDuckGo Images
duckduckgo_images.description: Search DuckDuckGo Images API. Retrieve image results with titles, sources, original links, thumbnails, and dimensions in JSON format.

params.name: q
params.doc: This parameter is used for the terms you want to search on DuckDuckGo Images.

params.name: locale
params.doc: Specifies the country and language for your search. The default parameter is us-en. Check the full list of supported DuckDuckGo locales.

params.name: time_period
params.doc: Filters results by date. Available values are: any_time Default

params.name: size
params.doc: Filters images by size. Available values are: small

params.name: color
params.doc: Filters images by color. Available values are: color

params.name: image_type
params.doc: Filters images by type. Available values are: photo

params.name: layout
params.doc: Filters images by layout. Available values are: square

params.name: license
params.doc: Filters images by license. Available values are: any

params.name: next_page_token
params.doc: This parameter is used to retrieve the next page of results. It is returned in the response when there are more results to display.

duckduckgo_light.name: DuckDuckGo Light Search
duckduckgo_light.description: Fast and lightweight DuckDuckGo search API. Retrieve organic results, ads, and knowledge graph with pagination support for any locale and time period.

params.name: q
params.doc: Parameter defines the query you want to search. You can use any search terms or phrases, such as "best coffee shops" or "machine learning".

params.name: locale
params.doc: Specifies the country and language for your search. The default parameter is us-en. Check the full list of supported DuckDuckGo locales.

params.name: time_period
params.doc: Filters results by date. Predefined values are: any_time Default

params.name: next_page_token
params.doc: Token for retrieving the next page of results. Located inside pagination.next_page_token in the response.

duckduckgo_videos.name: DuckDuckGo Videos
duckduckgo_videos.description: Search DuckDuckGo Videos API. Retrieve video results with titles, links, sources, channels, views, durations, and thumbnails in JSON.

params.name: q
params.doc: This parameter is used for the terms you want to search on DuckDuckGo Videos.

params.name: locale
params.doc: Specifies the country and language for your search. The default parameter is us-en. Check the full list of supported DuckDuckGo locales.

params.name: time_period
params.doc: Filters results by date. Available values are: any_time Default

params.name: duration
params.doc: Filters videos by duration. Available values are: short - Under 5 minutes

params.name: resolution
params.doc: Filters videos by resolution. Available values are: high - HD quality

params.name: license
params.doc: Filters videos by license. Available values are: creative_common - Creative Commons licensed

params.name: next_page_token
params.doc: This parameter is used to retrieve the next page of results. It is returned in the response when there are more results to display.

ebay_product.name: eBay Product
ebay_product.description: Retrieve eBay product data with pricing information and more. Access product data directly via API queries.

params.name: item_id
params.doc: This parameter specifies the id of the eBay Item you want to retrieve data for. It is optional when product_id is present. An item in eBay is a live listing (one seller’s offer) identified by an item_id. If the listing has ended or the item is no longer available, the request may automatically fall back to the corresponding product page.

params.name: product_id
params.doc: This parameter specifies the id of the eBay Product you want to retrieve data for. It is optional when item_id is present. Both can be used together if you want an specific item of said product, but the item page takes precedence. A product in eBay is a catalog record (canonical description of the thing) identified by an ePID, that can have multiple items from different sellers. For example a product Smartphone Brand X Model Y (with its specifications for hardware, battery, etc.) with its multiple items (with different sellers, prices, shipping, conditions, etc.). A product page shows information about the product and might contain information from one its items.

params.name: ebay_domain
params.doc: The default parameter ebay.com defines the eBay domain of the search and it's used for multiple countries, but other country-specific domains are also supported. Check the full list of supported eBay domains.

params.name: country
params.doc: A two-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code that allows you to set the delivery country for the product or item and change the language and currency of the page (if available). The default will be the domain's country. Check the full list of supported eBay countries.

params.name: delivery_country
params.doc: A two-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code that allows you to set the an specific delivery country for the search. The default will be country if it's set, otherwise it will be the domain's country. Check the full list of supported eBay delivery countries.

params.name: postal_code
params.doc: This parameter allows you to set the shipping postal code along with delivery_country for the search. It is not available for all delivery countries, check the full list of delivery countries that support postal codes, if not provided in those countries, eBay might automatically set a postal code.

ebay_search.name: eBay Search
ebay_search.description: Retrieve eBay search results with pricing information and more. Access product data directly via API queries.

params.name: q
params.doc: This parameter specifies your search query. It accepts any term or phrase you'd typically input in eBay search. This parameter is optional when the parameter category_id is present. The results will include only products containing all specified words, but you can refine your search by using: Commas and parentheses to get products that include any of the terms (e.g., (ring,earrings,necklace)). You can have multiple sets (e.g., (blue,red)(t-shirt,trousers), which would return products that include (blue or red) and (t-shirt or trousers).

params.name: category_id
params.doc: This parameter that allows you to restrict your search to a specific eBay category. Categories are different for each eBay domain. Category ids can be retrieved using the API or by inspecting category links found in ebay_domain/n/all-categories. Each category link follows the pattern ebay_domain/b/category_name/category_id/.

params.name: ebay_domain
params.doc: The default parameter ebay.com defines the eBay domain of the search and it's used for multiple countries, but other country-specific domains are also supported. Check the full list of supported eBay domains.

params.name: country
params.doc: Since eBay does not have domains for all countries, country is a two-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code that allows you to localize ebay.com and change the language and currency (if available). It defaults to the domain's country. Check the full list of supported eBay countries.

params.name: delivery_country
params.doc: A two-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code that allows you to set the an specific delivery country for the search. The default will be country if it's set, otherwise it will be the domain's country. Check the full list of supported eBay delivery countries.

params.name: postal_code
params.doc: This parameter allows you to set the shipping postal code along with delivery_country for the search. It is not available for all delivery countries, check the full list of delivery countries that support postal codes, if not provided in those countries, eBay might automatically set a postal code.

params.name: distance_radius
params.doc: A numerical value to filter results based on their distance to a given postal code. This parameter is only applicable when the parameter postal_code is also included.

params.name: product_origin_country
params.doc: A two-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code that allows you to filter products by the country they are located in and will be shipped from. Check the full list of supported eBay product origin countries.

params.name: price_min
params.doc: This parameter controls the minimum price of the products returned. For instance - 10 value would return products with a minimum price of 10.

params.name: price_max
params.doc: This parameter controls the maximum price of the products returned. For instance - 20.5 value would return products with a maximum price of 20.5.

params.name: condition
params.doc: This parameter allows you to filter items by their condition. Multiple conditions can be applied by separating them with commas (e.g., new,used_very_good). Available conditions include: new, new_opened, like_new, new_with_defects

params.name: buying_format
params.doc: This parameter allows you to filter search results by eBay's buying formats: auction, buy_it_now, best_offer.

params.name: preferred_location
params.doc: This parameter defines the preferred location of sellers: domestic, regional, worldwide.

params.name: include_related_results
params.doc: When set to true, the API returns eBay's "Results matching fewer words" items under a separate related_results key for queries that have no exact matches. Defaults to false and returns an error when no exact matches are found.

params.name: filters
params.doc: This parameter allows you to filter search results by various criteria. Multiple filters can be applied by separating them with commas (e.g., sale_items,free_shipping). Available filters include: Listing filters: sale_items

params.name: advanced_filters
params.doc: Advanced filters are specific to each product category, such as size and color for the Shirts category. These filters are expressed as key-value pairs separated by an equals sign (e.g., Size Type=Regular,Size=XS|S,Brand=adidas). You can apply multiple advanced filters by separating them with commas. The available advanced filters can be found via the API under the filters key. Some filters may be dependent on other filters. For example, the Size Type filter must be applied together with the Size filter.

params.name: sort_by
params.doc: This parameter allows sorting search results by different criteria. Below is the list of available sorting options: best_match Default

params.name: layout
params.doc: This parameter determines the layout of the search results. The possible values are: list and grid.

params.name: num
params.doc: This parameter determines the number of items per page. The possible values are: 60, 120 and 240. It defaults to 60.

params.name: page
params.doc: This parameter determines the results page number. It defaults to 1.

facebook_business_page.name: Facebook Business Page About Section
facebook_business_page.description: Retrieve Facebook Business Page information including contact details, hours, services, and about section data using page ID. Simple API for developers.

params.name: page_id
params.doc: The Facebook page ID. You can find it in the page URL (e.g., 100089525329756).

params.name: username
params.doc: The Facebook page username path. You can find it in the page URL (e.g., marcopoloristorante).

params.name: url
params.doc: A full Facebook page URL. Accepts direct page URLs (https://www.facebook.com/starbucks/), profile.php?id= URLs, /pages/<name>/<id> URLs, and mobile app share links (https://www.facebook.com/share/<token>/). Share links are resolved to their canonical target automatically. Note: You must provide exactly one of page_id, username, or url.

facebook_business_page_reviews.name: Facebook Business Page Reviews
facebook_business_page_reviews.description: Access detailed Facebook Business Page Reviews data including ratings, comments, and user information.

params.name: page_id
params.doc: The unique numeric ID of the Facebook Business Page.

params.name: username
params.doc: The username (vanity URL) of the Facebook Business Page.

params.name: url
params.doc: A full Facebook page URL. Accepts direct page URLs (https://www.facebook.com/starbucks/), profile.php?id= URLs, /pages/<name>/<id> URLs, and mobile app share links (https://www.facebook.com/share/<token>/). Share links are resolved to their canonical target automatically. Note: Provide exactly one of page_id, username, or url (or a next_page_token for pagination).

params.name: next_page_token
params.doc: A token for fetching the next set of reviews. You can obtain this token from the pagination.next_page_token field in the previous response.

gemini.name: Gemini
gemini.description: Access Google Gemini answers in structured JSON—text blocks, markdown, cited grounding reference links, inline images, inline YouTube videos, and typed cards.

params.name: q
params.doc: This parameter is used for the terms you want to ask Gemini. The answer is returned in the same language as your query - for example, queries in German will receive answers in German, queries in Spanish will receive answers in Spanish.

github_search.name: GitHub Search
github_search.description: Scrape GitHub search across ten verticals, from repositories and users to packages and marketplace. Real-time results in JSON with the GitHub Search API.

params.name: q
params.doc: The search query. Supports GitHub's search qualifier syntax, e.g. language:ruby stars:>1000 topic:cli for repositories, or is:pr is:merged for issues.

params.name: type
params.doc: The GitHub search vertical to query. Each type returns its own result shape. Options are: repositories - repositories (default)

params.name: sort
params.doc: Sorts the results by the given field. By default, results are ranked by GitHub's Best match relevance. The available values depend on type: repositories: stars, forks, help_wanted_issues, updated

params.name: order
params.doc: Sort direction. Requires sort — sending order on its own is rejected with a 400 error rather than ignored. Options are desc (default) and asc.

params.name: page
params.doc: The page of results to return. GitHub serves 10 results per page, up to page 100 (the first 1,000 results).

google.name: Google Search
google.description: Localize your search to any geographic location. Scrape organic results, ads, related searches, questions and more.

params.name: q
params.doc: This parameter is used for the terms you want to search on Google. Queries can include operators and advanced filters like "machine learning models", site:, inurl:, intitle:, AND, or OR.

params.name: kgmid
params.doc: Defines a Knowledge Graph identifier (kgmid), representing entities in Google's Knowledge Graph. Format: Location Identifier (/m/): Typically followed by 2 to 7 characters. Used primarily to represent specific locations. Find the identifier by searching for the "Freebase ID" on Wikidata. Example: kgmid=/m/02_286 refers to New York.

params.name: device
params.doc: The default parameter desktop defines the search on a desktop device. The mobile parameter defines the search on a mobile device. The tablet parameter defines the search on a tablet device.

params.name: location
params.doc: This parameter is used to specify the canonical location of the search. For exact targeting or to see all available options, check out the Locations API. If multiple locations match your input, the most popular one will be selected. For example - location=New York would select New York,United States or location=London would select London TV Region,England,United Kingdom.

params.name: uule
params.doc: This parameter sets the exact Google-encoded location for the search, and uule and location cannot be used at the same time. SearchApi builds it for you when you use the location parameter, but you can provide your own if you want precise control.

params.name: latitude
params.doc: Latitude of the search location, in decimal degrees (-90 to 90). Use with longitude. Cannot be combined with location or uule.

params.name: longitude
params.doc: Longitude of the search location, in decimal degrees (-180 to 180). Use with latitude. Cannot be combined with location or uule.

params.name: google_domain
params.doc: As of Apr 15, 2025, Google began phasing out country code top-level domains (ccTLDs). Users using the search bar or visiting local domains like google.de or google.co.uk are now automatically redirected to google.com. For localized searches, use the gl (country), hl (language) or other localization parameters instead. Learn more in Google's official announcement. See the full list of supported Google domains.

params.name: gl
params.doc: The default parameter us defines the country of the search. Check the full list of supported Google gl countries. When latitude and longitude are used, gl is inferred from the coordinates, and coordinates in a country this engine does not support are rejected.

params.name: hl
params.doc: The default parameter en defines the interface language of the search. Check the full list of supported Google hl languages.

params.name: lr
params.doc: The lr parameter restricts search results to documents written in a particular language or a set of languages. The accepted format for this parameter is lang_{2-letter country code}. For instance, to filter documents written in Japanese, the value should be set to lang_jp. To incorporate multiple languages, a value like lang_it|lang_de restricts the search to documents written in either Italian or German. Google identifies the document language based on the top-level domain (TLD) of the document's URL, any language meta tags present, or the language utilized within the document's body text. Check the full list of supported Google lr languages.

params.name: cr
params.doc: The cr parameter restricts search results to documents originating in a particular country. Google determines the country of a document by the top-level domain (TLD) of the document's URL or by Web server's IP address geographic location. Check the full list of supported Google cr countries.

params.name: nfpr
params.doc: This parameter controls whether results from queries that have been auto-corrected for spelling errors are included. To exclude these auto-corrected results, set the value to 1. By default, the value is 0, meaning auto-corrected results are included.

params.name: filter
params.doc: This parameter controls whether the "Duplicate Content" and "Host Crowding" filters are enabled. Set the value to 1 to enable these filters, which is the default setting. To disable these filters, set the value to 0.

params.name: safe
params.doc: This parameter toggles the SafeSearch feature for the results. SafeSearch operates by filtering out adult content from your search results. Google's filters use proprietary technology to check keywords, phrases and URLs. While no filters are 100 percent accurate, SafeSearch will remove the overwhelming majority of adult content from your search results. Supported values are active to enable strict SafeSearch, blur to blur explicit images, and off to disable SafeSearch. By default, the value is blur.

params.name: time_period
params.doc: This parameter restricts results to URLs based on date. Supported values are: last_1_minute - data from the past minute.

params.name: time_period_min
params.doc: This parameter specifies the start of the time period. It could be used in combination with the time_period_max parameter. The value should be in the format MM/DD/YYYY.

params.name: time_period_max
params.doc: This parameter specifies the end of the time period. It could be used in combination with the time_period_min parameter. The value should be in the format MM/DD/YYYY.

params.name: verbatim
params.doc: This parameter forces Google to use your exact keywords, bypassing automatic spelling corrections, synonyms, and personalized or stemmed variations. Set the value to true to enable. Can be combined with time_period filters. Note: Verbatim mode is stricter than the nfpr parameter — it disables all query modifications, not just spelling corrections. If you only want to prevent spelling auto-correction while keeping other Google features, use nfpr=1 instead.

params.name: num
params.doc: Phased out by Google on September 2025. It is now constant 10. Check the Google Rank Tracking API for num=100 support.

params.name: page
params.doc: This parameter indicates which page of results to return. By default, it is set to 1.

params.name: optimization_strategy
params.doc: Controls how the search request is optimized. Available options: performance Default

params.name: link
params.doc: Controls how Google's encrypted redirect links (https://www.google.com/goto?url=...) are returned. These appear in AI Overview and People Also Ask reference links, sitelinks, perspectives, knowledge graph profiles and video key moments; organic result links are recovered from the page where possible. By default (raw) the remaining redirects are returned as-is. Set it to resolved to have each one followed to its destination URL. Resolving is best-effort and adds latency; a redirect that cannot be resolved stays as the redirect URL.

google_about_this_domain.name: Google About This Domain
google_about_this_domain.description: Get source information, indexing dates, and related web results for any domain. Access Google's About This Result feature via API.

params.name: domain
params.doc: The domain you want to get information about. For example: airbnb.com.

params.name: gl
params.doc: Defines the country of the search. Check the full list of supported Google gl countries.

params.name: hl
params.doc: The default parameter en defines the interface language of the search. Check the full list of supported Google hl languages.

google_about_this_store.name: Google About This Store
google_about_this_store.description: Retrieve store ratings, reviews, badges, review categories, and social profiles from Google's About This Store page via API.

params.name: domain
params.doc: The domain you want to get information about. For example: walmart.com.

params.name: gl
params.doc: The default parameter us defines the country of the search. Check the full list of supported Google gl countries.

params.name: hl
params.doc: The default parameter en defines the interface language of the search. Check the full list of supported Google hl languages.

params.name: sort_by
params.doc: Sorts the reviews. Supported values: newest, most_helpful.

params.name: rating
params.doc: Filters reviews by star rating. Supported values: 5, 4, 3, 2, 1.

params.name: time_period
params.doc: Filters reviews by time period. Supported values: last_six_months, last_year, last_five_years.

params.name: reviews_next_page_token
params.doc: Parameter defines the token used to retrieve the next page of reviews. It can be retrieved on the previous page. It carries the parameters and filters from the original search, but explicit values still take precedence if needed. Each paginated request returns up to 10 reviews. The token is omitted on the final page.

google_ads_advertiser_info.name: Google Ads Advertiser Info
google_ads_advertiser_info.description: Retrieve Google advertiser data, including advertiser name, location, and ad transparency links, with the Google Ads Advertiser Info API.

params.name: advertiser_info_token
params.doc: To retrieve its value, follow these steps Perform a search using our Google Search API.

google_ads_transparency_center.name: Google Ads Transparency Center
google_ads_transparency_center.description: Scrape Google Ads Transparency Center data including advertiser info, ad creatives, and campaign details. Retrieve detailed JSON data.

params.name: advertiser_id
params.doc: Specifies the advertiser's unique ID. Multiple IDs can be provided, separated by commas. Required if domain is not provided. You can obtain the advertiser_id in two ways: Use our Advertiser Search API to search for advertisers or domain by keyword.

params.name: domain
params.doc: Defines the advertiser's verified domain (e.g., tesla.com). Required if advertiser_id is not provided.

params.name: region
params.doc: Specifies the region for your search. The default parameter is anywhere. Check the full list of supported Google Ads Transparency Center regions.

params.name: platform
params.doc: Specifies the platform for which the ads are being retrieved. Accepted values include:google_play, google_maps, google_search, youtube, or google_shopping.

params.name: ad_format
params.doc: Filters results based on ad format. Accepted values are: text, image, or video.

params.name: time_period
params.doc: Limits the results to a specific time range. Accepted values are: today yesteday last_7_days last_30_days Alternatively, specify a custom range using YYYY-MM-DD..YYYY-MM-DD.

params.name: next_page_token
params.doc: A token for fetching the next set of results. You can obtain this token from the next_page_token field in the previous response

params.name: num
params.doc: Specifies the number of results to return. Default is 40. The maximum is 100.

google_ads_transparency_center_ad_detail.name: Google Ads Transparency Center Ad Details
google_ads_transparency_center_ad_detail.description: Scrape Google Ads Transparency Center data including advertiser info, ad creatives, and campaign details. Retrieve detailed JSON data.

params.name: advertiser_id
params.doc: Specifies the advertiser's unique ID. You can obtain the advertiser_id in two ways: Use our Advertiser Search API to search for advertisers or domain by keyword.

params.name: creative_id
params.doc: Specifies the creative's unique ID. You can obtain the creative_id in two ways: Use our Google Ads Transparency Center API to retrieve the creative ID directly.

google_ads_transparency_center_advertise.name: Google Ads Transparency Center Advertiser Search
google_ads_transparency_center_advertise.description: Search for advertisers in Google Ads Transparency Center on a given keyword. Access advertiser details including names, regions, ID's, and number of ads.

params.name: q
params.doc: Specifies the keyword to search for advertisers or domains.

params.name: region
params.doc: Specifies the region for your search. The default parameter is anywhere. Check the full list of supported Google Ads Transparency Center regions.

params.name: num_advertisers
params.doc: Specifies the number of advertisers to return. The default is 10. The maximum is 100.

params.name: num_domains
params.doc: Specifies the number of domains to return. The default is 10. The maximum is 100.

google_ai_mode.name: Google AI Mode
google_ai_mode.description: Access detailed Google AI Mode data. Retrieve results in JSON format.

params.name: q
params.doc: This parameter is used for the terms you want to search on Google AI Mode. The AI Mode will respond in the same language as your query - for example, queries in German will receive answers in German, queries in Spanish will receive answers in Spanish. params.name: gl

params.name: hl

google_ai_overview.name: Google AI Overview
google_ai_overview.description: Access Google's AI-powered search overviews with structured data, markdown formatting, and reference links using the Google AI Overview API.

params.name: q

params.doc: This parameter identifies the client initiating the autocomplete request. For instance, using chrome as the value signifies that the request comes from the Chrome browser. params.doc: The cp parameter is used to determine the cursor position within the search query for autocomplete requests. The location of the cursor is important as it affects the suggestions provided by the autocomplete feature of the API.

params.name: time_period
params.doc: This parameter restricts results to URLs based on date. Supported values are: 21century - data from 2000 till 2099.

params.name: time_period_max

params.name: q
params.doc: Free-text prompt describing the kind of destinations you want (e.g. beaches and islands, places with great food, ski trips). Google's AI interprets the prompt and curates the deals to matching destinations, replacing the default "cheapest anywhere" spread. Google honors a prompt or the filters, never both, so combining it with max_price, included_airlines, a stops other than any, a travel_class other than economy, or a passenger count above its default is rejected with a 400 rather than answered with unfiltered results.

params.name: children

params.name: infants_in_seat

params.name: infants_on_lap

params.name: cr

params.name: sort_by

params.name: nfpr

params.name: filter

params.name: page

params.name: q
params.doc: This parameter is used for the terms you want to search on Google Patents. Queries can include operators and advanced filters like "artificial intelligence", AND, or OR. For more advanced syntax, refer to the official Google documentation on Google Patents search query syntax.

params.name: countries
params.doc: Parameter filters results by country. Use the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, e.g., US for the United States, DE for Germany. To use multiple countries, separate them with a comma ,. For example: US,DE. Check the full list of supported Google Patents countries.

params.name: language
params.doc: Parameter filters results by language. To specify multiple languages, separate them with a comma ,. params.name: patent_status
params.doc: Parameter filters patent results by status. Use GRANT for granted patents and APPLICATION for patent applications.

params.name: patent_type
params.doc: Parameter filters patent results by type. Use PATENT for patents, DESIGN for design patents.

params.name: litigation
params.doc: Parameter filterss patent results by litigation status. Use YES to include results with related litigation, NO to exclude them.

params.name: clustered
params.doc: Parameter groups the results by classification. Set the value to true to enable clustering.

params.name: dups
params.doc: Parameter defines how duplicates are handled. The default value is family. Alternatively, use language to filter duplicates based on publication.

params.name: sort
params.doc: Parameter controls the sorting order. The default is relevance. Other options include: new - Sort by filing date for patents, and by publication date for scholarly results.

params.name: patents
params.doc: Parameter controls the inclusion of patent results. Set to false to exclude patents. Default value is true.

params.name: scholar
params.doc: Parameter controls the inclusion of scholarly results. Set to true to include scholarly results. Default value is false.

params.name: inventor
params.doc: Parameter filters results by inventor names. To specify multiple inventors, separate them with a comma ,. For example: John Doe,Jane Doe.

params.name: assignee
params.doc: Parameter filters results by assignee names. To specify multiple assignees, separate them with a comma ,. For example: Apple Inc,Google LLC.

params.name: before

params.name: after

params.name: num

params.name: page
params.doc: This parameter indicates which page of results to return. By default, it is set to 1. Use in combination with the num parameter to implement pagination.

params.name: num

params.name: link

google_scholar.name: Google Scholar
google_scholar.description: Scrape Google Scholar educational resources with a real-time Google Scholar Scraper API. Search for articles and patents in any state or federal court.

params.name: q
params.doc: This parameter is used for the terms you want to search in Google Scholar. Queries can include operators and advanced filters like "quantum computing", author:, or source:. Parameter is not required if cites or cluster parameter is present.

params.name: cites
params.doc: The cites parameter is used to specify a unique ID for an article. Utilizing this parameter will generate a list of documents in Google Scholar that cite the specified article. For instance, cites=13392090434137936466 could be used to find all documents that cite the article with this unique ID. Additionally, using both the cites and q parameters together will result in a search within the citing articles themselves.

params.name: cluster
params.doc: The cluster parameter is used to specify a unique ID for an article. Utilizing this parameter will generate a list of document versions in Google Scholar that are related to the specified article. Note: When the q and cluster parameters are used together, they are not compatible. In such cases, priority is given to the q parameter.

params.name: hl
params.doc: The default parameter en defines the interface language of the search. Check the full list of supported Google hl languages.

params.name: lr
params.doc: The lr parameter restricts search results to documents written in a particular language or a set of languages. The accepted format for this parameter is lang_{2-letter country code}. For instance, to filter documents written in Japanese, the value should be set to lang_jp. To incorporate multiple languages, a value like lang_it|lang_de restricts the search to documents written in either Italian or German. Google identifies the document language based on the top-level domain (TLD) of the document's URL, any language meta tags present, or the language utilized within the document's body text. Check the full list of supported Google lr languages.

params.name: scisbd
params.doc: Default value 0 returns all results sorted by relevance. There are two other options: 1 - includes only abstracts, filters articles added in the last year, and sorts by date.

params.name: as_ylo
params.doc: Parameter sets the start year to filter results. Pair with as_yhi for a specific end year. Input format: YYYY. E.g., as_ylo=2022 fetches results from 2022 onwards.

params.name: as_yhi
params.doc: Parameter sets the start year to filter results. Pair with as_yhi for a specific end year. Input format: YYYY. E.g., as_yhi=2022 fetches results till 2022 backwards.

params.name: as_rr
params.doc: Default value 0 returns all results. Use 1 to return results only with review articles.

params.name: as_vis
params.doc: Default value 0 returns results with citations. Use 1 to return results without citations.

params.name: as_sdt
params.doc: This parameter works as a filter for patents or as filter for US court law. By default, 0 returns results without patents. Patent Filter Values: 0 - Excludes patents (default).

params.name: filter
params.doc: This parameter controls whether the "Duplicate Content" and "Host Crowding" filters are enabled. Set the value to 1 to enable these filters, which is the default setting. To disable these filters, set the value to 0.

params.name: source
params.doc: This parameter allows filtering of organic results based on a specific source. It is added to the q parameter and is not compatible with cites or cluster parameters.

params.name: num
params.doc: This parameter specifies the number of results to display per page. By default, it is set to 10, maximum number - 20. Use in combination with the page parameter to implement pagination functionality.

params.name: page
params.doc: This parameter indicates which page of results to return. By default, it is set to 1. Use in combination with the num parameter to implement pagination.

params.name: author_id
params.doc: The parameter specifies the author_id for your search. Locate these values in: The URL of a Google Scholar page: https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=author_id.

params.name: citation_id

params.name: hl
params.doc: The default parameter en defines the interface language of the search. Check the full list of supported Google hl languages.

params.name: sortby
params.doc: Articles are sorted by the number of citations by default. If you wish to: Sort by date, use: sortby=pubdate.

params.name: view_op
params.doc: The parameter specifies the search type. By default, it provides detailed information about an author. Here are the available options:: view_citation - Provides in-depth citation details. A citation_id is required.

params.name: agencyid
params.doc: Use this parameter to sort mandates by agency, using the unique agencyid. To find these values, refer to the JSON responses when employing the view_op=list_mandates parameter.

params.name: page
params.doc: Parameter indicates which page of results to return. By default, it is set to 1. Parameter is only used while view_op parameter is empty or is set to list_mandates

params.doc: Defines the Google Scholar case identifier. Obtain it from the organic_results.caselaw_id field returned by the Google Scholar API when searching in case-law mode (as_sdt), or from the referenced_cases.caselaw_id field of any other Google Scholar Case Law response.

params.name: hl

params.name: q
params.doc: Specifies the search query, similar to performing a regular Google search. Filters embedded in the q parameter act as hints rather than strict filters. params.doc: Applies strict filtering rules based on encoded values. Example: CAEYFyoDcHM1MhwIFxISUHJpY2U6IGxvdyB0byBoaWdoKgQQARgBYAKIAQE sorts products by price (low to high). Filters provided in the JSON response can be used in subsequent requests to apply additional filters iteratively.

params.name: price_min
params.doc: Specifies the minimum price of the products returned. This parameter must include the currency. For example, 2.50 filters results to products priced at $2.50 or higher. Must be used as a strict filter before applying shoprs.

params.name: price_max
params.doc: Specifies the maximum price of the products returned. This parameter must include the currency. For example, 100 filters results to products priced at $100 or less. Must be used as a strict filter before applying shoprs.

params.name: is_on_sale
params.doc: Filters results to show only products that are currently on sale. Set to true to show only discounted items. Can be combined with is_small_business, is_free_delivery, and sort_by for more refined searches. Note: If the shoprs parameter is provided, it takes priority and this parameter will be ignored.

params.name: is_small_business
params.doc: Filters results to show only products sold by small businesses. Set to true to show only small business sellers. Can be combined with is_on_sale, is_free_delivery, and sort_by for more refined searches. Note: If the shoprs parameter is provided, it takes priority and this parameter will be ignored.

params.name: is_free_delivery
params.doc: Filters results to show only products with free shipping available. Set to true to show only items that offer free shipping. Can be combined with is_on_sale, is_small_business, and sort_by for more refined searches. Note: If the shoprs parameter is provided, it takes priority and this parameter will be ignored.

params.name: sort_by
params.doc: Sorts the shopping results by the specified criteria. Available options: price_low_to_high - Sort products from lowest to highest price

params.name: condition
params.doc: Filters product condition. Options include: new for new products, and used for used items.

params.name: include_favicon
params.doc: This parameter includes the seller's favicon in the shopping results. It is set to false by default. Set it to true to include favicons.

params.name: include_base_images
params.doc: This parameter includes base64-encoded product images in the shopping results. It is set to false by default. Set it to true to include base64 images.

params.name: page
params.doc: Indicates which page of results to return. The default is 1.

params.name: link
params.doc: Controls how product ad links are returned. On some searches Google encrypts each ad's link as a redirect (https://www.google.com/goto?url=...). By default (raw) those redirects are returned as-is. Set it to resolved to have each one followed to the merchant URL. Resolving is best-effort and adds latency; a redirect that cannot be resolved stays as the redirect URL. The merchant domain is returned either way.

params.name: nfpr

params.name: filter

params.name: safe
params.doc: This parameter toggles the SafeSearch feature for the results. SafeSearch operates by filtering out adult content from your search results. Google's filters use proprietary technology to check keywords, phrases and URLs. While no filters are 100 percent accurate, SafeSearch will remove the overwhelming majority of adult content from your search results. Supported values are active to enable strict SafeSearch, blur to blur explicit images, and off to disable SafeSearch. By default, the value is blur.

params.name: tbs
params.doc: This parameter restricts results to URLs based on encoded values.

params.name: time_period

params.name: quality
params.doc: This parameter restricts results to URLs based on video quality. By default, all videos are returned. To retrieve only videos with high quality, high param should be used. Note: this parameter is not compatible with a custom tbs parameter.

params.name: captioned
params.doc: This parameter restricts results to URLs based on video captions. By default, all videos are returned. To retrieve only videos with closed caption, set this parameter to closed. Note: this parameter is not compatible with a custom tbs parameter.

params.name: source
params.doc: This parameter restricts results to URLs based on source. Supported values are: instagram, tiktok, youtube, facebook, x, bluestone. Note: this parameter is not compatible with a custom tbs parameter.

params.name: page

google_travel_explore.name: Google Travel Explore
google_travel_explore.description: Google Travel Explore API provides a powerful way to explore flight destinations based on flexible search parameters.

params.name: departure_id
params.doc: This parameter specifies the code for the departure airport or a location identifier. Available options can be: Airport Code: A 3-letter code representing the departure airport (e.g., MAD for Madrid-Barajas Airport or JFK for John F. Kennedy International Airport). You can find these codes using resources like Google Flights or IATA.

params.name: arrival_id
params.doc: This parameter specifies the code for the arrival location identifier. Available options can be: Location Identifier (kgmid): A string that begins with /m/, used to represent a specific location. You can find this identifier on Wikidata by looking for the "Freebase ID" while searching for location. While Google Flights also supports kgmid, this API allows you to search broader geographical regions that aren't available in Google Flights. params.name: data_type
params.doc: Parameter defines the data type you wish to search for. You have several options to choose from: TIMESERIES also known as Interest Over Time, used to return historical, indexed data for a given input.

params.name: cat

params.name: region

params.name: geo
params.doc: The default value for the location parameter is set to Worldwide, which denotes a global scope for the search. This parameter specifies the geographical area for the query search. If it is not explicitly set, the search defaults to a worldwide range. Check the full list of supported Google Trends geo locations.

params.name: tz
params.doc: Parameter defines timezone offset (the difference in hours and minutes between a particular time zone and UTC). Could be selected from -1439 to 1439. Default - 420.

google_trends_autocomplete.description: Scrape real-time Google Trends Autocomplete results. Retrieve search id, title, type and link.

params.name: q
params.doc: This parameter is used for the terms you want autocomplete suggestions for in Google Trends. You must type at least 3 characters to get the results.

params.name: hl
params.doc: The default parameter en defines the language of the store. Check the full list of supported Google hl languages.

google_trends_trending_now.name: Google Trends Trending Now
google_trends_trending_now.description: Access trending queries with the Google Trends Trending Now API. Get trending topics, keywords, and their search volume.

params.name: geo
params.doc: Specifies the geographical area for the search, with the default set to US. For a full list of supported locations, refer to the Google Trends Trending Now geo locations.

params.name: time
params.doc: Filters trending queries based on the specified time duration. Available options: past_4_hours

google_trends_trending_now_news.name: Google Trends Trending Now News
google_trends_trending_now_news.description: Retrieve news articles related to trending search queries with the Google Trends Trending Now News API.

params.name: news_token
params.doc: To retrieve the news_token, follow these steps: Make a search request using our Google Trends Trending Now API.

google_videos.name: Google Videos
google_videos.description: Scrape Google videos using Google Videos Scraper API. Retrieve videos, video carousel, and shorts formatted as JSON results.

params.name: q
params.doc: This parameter is used for the terms you want to search on Google Videos. Queries can include operators and advanced filters like "cooking tutorials", site:, inurl:, intitle:, as_dt, or as_eq.

params.name: device
params.doc: The default parameter desktop defines the search on a desktop device. The mobile parameter defines the search on a mobile device. The tablet parameter defines the search on a tablet device.

params.name: location
params.doc: This parameter is used to specify the canonical location of the search. For exact targeting or to see all available options, check out the Locations API. If multiple locations match your input, the most popular one will be selected.

params.name: uule
params.doc: This parameter sets the exact Google-encoded location for the search, and uule and location cannot be used at the same time. SearchApi builds it for you when you use the location parameter, but you can provide your own if you want precise control.

params.name: google_domain
params.doc: As of Apr 15, 2025, Google began phasing out country code top-level domains (ccTLDs). Users using the search bar or visiting local domains like google.de or google.co.uk are now automatically redirected to google.com. For localized searches, use the gl (country), hl (language) or other localization parameters instead. Learn more in Google's official announcement. See the full list of supported Google domains.

params.name: gl
params.doc: The default parameter us defines the country of the search. Check the full list of supported Google gl countries.

params.name: hl
params.doc: The default parameter en defines the interface language of the search. Check the full list of supported Google hl languages.

params.name: lr
params.doc: The lr parameter restricts search results to documents written in a particular language or a set of languages. The accepted format for this parameter is lang_{2-letter country code}. For instance, to filter documents written in Japanese, the value should be set to lang_jp. To incorporate multiple languages, a value like lang_it|lang_de restricts the search to documents written in either Italian or German. Google identifies the document language based on the top-level domain (TLD) of the document's URL, any language meta tags present, or the language utilized within the document's body text. Check the full list of supported Google lr languages.

params.name: cr
params.doc: The cr parameter restricts search results to documents originating in a particular country. Google determines the country of a document by the top-level domain (TLD) of the document's URL or by Web server's IP address geographic location. Check the full list of supported Google cr countries.

params.name: nfpr
params.doc: This parameter controls whether results from queries that have been auto-corrected for spelling errors are included. To exclude these auto-corrected results, set the value to 1. By default, the value is 0, meaning auto-corrected results are included.

params.name: filter
params.doc: This parameter controls whether the "Duplicate Content" and "Host Crowding" filters are enabled. Set the value to 1 to enable these filters, which is the default setting. To disable these filters, set the value to 0.

params.name: safe
params.doc: This parameter toggles the SafeSearch feature for the results. SafeSearch operates by filtering out adult content from your search results. Google's filters use proprietary technology to check keywords, phrases and URLs. While no filters are 100 percent accurate, SafeSearch will remove the overwhelming majority of adult content from your search results. Supported values are active to enable strict SafeSearch, blur to blur explicit images, and off to disable SafeSearch. By default, the value is blur.

params.name: tbs
params.doc: This parameter restricts results to URLs based on encoded values. For instance, dur:s would return only results that are shorter than 4 min.

params.name: time_period
params.doc: This parameter restricts results to URLs based on date. Supported values are: last_hour - data from the past hour.

params.name: duration
params.doc: This parameter restricts results to URLs based on video duration. Supported values are: short - short videos (0-4 min.).

params.name: quality
params.doc: This parameter restricts results to URLs based on video quality. By default, all videos are returned. To retrieve only videos with high quality, high param should be used. Note: this parameter is not compatible with a custom tbs parameter.

params.name: captioned
params.doc: This parameter restricts results to URLs based on video captions. By default, all videos are returned. To retrieve only videos with closed caption, closed param should be used. Note: this parameter is not compatible with a custom tbs parameter.

params.name: source
params.doc: This parameter restricts results to URLs based on source. Supported values are: youtube, cncc, cnn, ted, cbsnews, twitter, tiktok, facebook, timesnownews, nbcnews, foxnews. Note: this parameter is not compatible with a custom tbs parameter.

params.name: link
params.doc: Controls how result links are returned. By default (raw), each result link is Google's redirect URL (https://www.google.com/goto?url=...). Set it to resolved to return the direct destination URL instead. Resolving follows each redirect, so it may add latency to the response.

params.name: page
params.doc: This parameter indicates which page of results to return. By default, it is set to 1.

instagram_comments.name: Instagram Comments
instagram_comments.description: Retrieve comments on any public Instagram post or reel. Get comment text, timestamps, like counts and author profiles as structured JSON.

params.name: post_id
params.doc: Parameter defines the unique identifier for the Instagram post you want comments for. A post can be either an image, carousel, or reel. You can find the identifier using the Instagram Profile API or in the post URL: https://www.instagram.com/p/DbTmwYKFkZo/ uses DbTmwYKFkZo, and https://www.instagram.com/reel/DbL6n0ggXDZ/ uses DbL6n0ggXDZ. The full post URL is also accepted.

params.name: next_page_token
params.doc: Parameter defines the cursor for the next page of comments. Take the value from pagination.next_page_token in a previous response and pass it back to page forward.

instagram_post.name: Instagram Post
instagram_post.description: Extract a public Instagram post or reel as JSON, including captions, authors, engagement, direct media URLs, tags, and carousel items.

params.name: post_id
params.doc: Parameter defines the unique identifier for the Instagram post you want to retrieve. A post can be either an image, carousel, or reel. You can find the identifier using the Instagram Profile API or in the post URL: https://www.instagram.com/p/DavpizrjugI/ uses DavpizrjugI, and https://www.instagram.com/reel/DRaV7mnAGq7/ uses DRaV7mnAGq7. The full post URL is also accepted.

instagram_profile.name: Instagram Profile
instagram_profile.description: Access detailed Instagram Profile data. Retrieve name, avatar, bio, followers, following, posts and more.

params.name: username
params.doc: Parameter defines the username of the Instagram profile you want to search.

linkedin_ad_library.name: LinkedIn Ad Library
linkedin_ad_library.description: Scrape LinkedIn Ad Library data including advertiser info, ad creatives, and campaign details. Retrieve detailed JSON data.

params.name: q
params.doc: Defines the keyword for your search. Use this parameter to search for ads containing specific keywords or phrases.

params.name: advertiser
params.doc: Specifies the advertiser name or company to search for. This will return ads from that specific advertiser.

params.name: country
params.doc: Specifies the country to filter ads by. Use comma-separated values for multiple countries (e.g., 'US,CA,GB'). Check the full list of supported LinkedIn Ad Library countries.

params.name: time_period
params.doc: Specifies the date range for ads. You can use predefined values like last_year, this_year, this_month, last_30_days, or custom date range in format YYYY-MM-DD..YYYY-MM-DD. Dates cannot be in the future (relative to UTC), and the start date cannot be earlier than one year ago.

params.name: next_page_token
params.doc: A token for fetching the next set of results. You can obtain this token from the next_page_token field in the previous response.

linkedin_ad_library_ad_details.name: LinkedIn Ad Library Ad Details
linkedin_ad_library_ad_details.description: Retrieve a single LinkedIn ad by ID, including run dates, estimated impressions, impressions by country, and ad targeting. Detailed JSON data.

params.name: ad_id
params.doc: Specifies the ad's unique ID, for example 870198506. Obtain it from the id field on each ad returned by the LinkedIn Ad Library API whose link points at an /ad-library/detail/ page. Employer-brand ads link to a different page this engine cannot fetch.

meta_ad_library.name: Meta Ad Library
meta_ad_library.description: Scrape Meta Ad Library data including advertiser info, ad creatives, and campaign details. Retrieve detailed JSON data.

params.name: q
params.doc: Defines the keyword for your search. When present together with page_id or location_id, it will filter that page or location for the keyword. Enclosing the whole query in double quotes searches for an exact phrase, for example q="air jordan". You can pass several quoted phrases, such as q="air jordan" "just do it", and each one is matched as a phrase. Mixing quoted and unquoted terms, for example q="air jordan" nike, is matched as unordered keywords. Use search_type to control this explicitly.

params.name: page_id
params.doc: Specifies the page's unique ID. You can obtain the page_id in two ways: Use our Page Search API to retrieve the page ID directly from Meta Ad Library.

params.name: location_id
params.doc: Filters ads based on a specific geographic location using Meta Ad Library's location targeting feature. This parameter must be used together with location_name and location_type to define the targeted area. All three values can be obtained using our Page Search API, which supports location search aligned with Meta Ad Library's internal targeting system.

params.name: country
params.doc: Specifies the country for your search. The default value is ALL. Check the full list of supported Meta Ad Library countries and their supported ad_type.

params.name: content_languages
params.doc: Comma-separated list of content languages to filter ads by. Check the full list of supported Meta Ad Library content languages.

params.name: ad_type
params.doc: Specifies the type of ads to return. Default is all. Supported values include: all, political_and_issue_ads, housing_ads, employment_ads, credit_ads. Note: Availability may depend on the selected country. Check the full list of supported Meta Ad Library countries and their supported ad_type.

params.name: active_status
params.doc: Filters ads by their status. Default is active. Supported values include: active, inactive, all.

params.name: search_type
params.doc: Controls how q is matched. Supported values are keyword_unordered, which matches ads containing all your keywords in any order, and keyword_exact_phrase, which matches quoted phrases exactly, respecting word order. When omitted, the type is inferred from q: a query made up entirely of quoted phrases uses keyword_exact_phrase, and anything else uses keyword_unordered. This parameter is ignored when page_id or location_id is present, since those searches use their own type.

params.name: media_type
params.doc: Filters results based on media type. Default is all. Supported values are: all, video, image, meme, image_and_meme, none.

params.name: platforms
params.doc: Comma-separated list of platforms where the ads appear. Supported values include: facebook, instagram, audience_network, messenger, threads.

params.name: start_date
params.doc: The earliest date to include ads from, in format YYYY-MM-DD. Cannot be in the future (relative to UTC).

params.name: end_date
params.doc: The latest date to include ads from, in format YYYY-MM-DD. Cannot be in the future (relative to UTC).

params.name: sort_by
params.doc: Specifies the sort order of results. Supported values are: most_recent, impressions_high_to_low. Default is impressions_high_to_low.

params.name: next_page_token
params.doc: A token for fetching the next set of results. You can obtain this token from the next_page_token field in the previous response.Note: Tokens can grow large (8KB+) after several pages. If you encounter 413 or 414 errors, use a POST request with the token in the JSON body instead of the URL query string.

meta_ad_library_ad_details.name: Meta Ad Library Ad Details
meta_ad_library_ad_details.description: Search for ads in Meta Ad Library on a given ad archive ID. Access ad European Union and UK Transparency insights.

params.name: ad_details_token
params.doc: Recommended. Obtain it from the ad_details_token field on each ad returned by the Meta Ad Library API. Using ad_details_token provides better results for extracting political ads and eu_transparency or uk_transparency data. Using ad_archive_id alone may not return results for all ads.

params.name: ad_archive_id
params.doc: Specifies the ad's unique ID. Required when ad_details_token is not provided. You can obtain it in two ways: Use our Meta Ad Library API. The ad_archive_id is included as a key for each ad object returned by the API.

meta_ad_library_page_info.name: Meta Ad Library Page Info
meta_ad_library_page_info.description: Retrieve page information from the Meta Ad Library including name, category, followers, transparency info, admin locations, and ad spend.

params.name: page_id
params.doc: Specifies the Facebook page ID to retrieve information for. You can obtain it in two ways: Use our Meta Ad Library Page Search API to search for a page by keyword and get its page_id.

meta_ad_library_page_search.name: Meta Ad Library Page Search
meta_ad_library_page_search.description: Search for pages in Meta Ad Library on a given keyword. Access page details including names, regions, ID's, and number of ads.

params.name: q
params.doc: Defines the keyword for your search.

params.name: country
params.doc: Specifies the country for your search. The default value is ALL. Check the full list of supported Meta Ad Library countries and their supported ad_type.

params.name: ad_type
params.doc: Specifies the type of ads to return. Default is all. Supported values include: all, political_and_issue_ads, housing_ads, employment_ads, credit_ads.
